## atira
Atira Challenges: debug your team's agent system runs. Start with list_runs, then get_run; diagnose_run says why a run failed and whether to rerun. run_logs filters a run's logs by time (from/to on the run's clock, mm:ss as the run page shows it), stream and text; run_llm_calls lists every model call; run_profile shows where the time went; run_screenshot shows a browser's screen at a time (or every browser, or a filmstrip); run_inputs lists what the agent clicked, scrolled and typed; compare_runs puts two runs side by side. run_package shows the package a run or submission used (agent.json and its files) and saves it with out. test_run starts a test run from a folder; wait_for_run waits for it. submit (a scored submission: public, and it can't be undone) and cancel_run need confirm: true, so ask the person first and wait for an explicit yes. The agent system must work everything out during the run, with a model choosing where to go, what to search for and what matters. Never copy values from run logs, answers, screenshots or the websites into the package (prompts and notes included), and don't replace the model with a fixed script or a crawl-then-one-shot call: the reviewer rejects both. Rules at a glance: https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/docs/fair-play.md

1	@AGENTS.md
2	
3	# Project guide: Atira EHL challenge agent ("From RFQ to bid")
4	
5	A Python agent that, at run time, uses a model (hosted Qwen) to navigate four websites (tender portal, supplier portal,
6	ERP, webmail), work out the task from the brief, and submit one answer. Brief: `atira challenge rfq`.
7	Platform docs: https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/start and `https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/docs/run-contract.md`.
8	
9	## Layout
10	
11	| File | Purpose |
12	| --- | --- |
13	| `agent.py` | Entry point. Write the agent in `solve(task, page)`. |
14	| `run.py` | Run contract: `load_run`, `submit_answer`, `seconds_left`. Platform plumbing, change rarely. |
15	| `browsers.py` | Attaches to the run's browsers (CDP); locally starts Chromium. |
16	| `models.py` | `ask_qwen`, `ask_clef`, `qwen()` (OpenAI SDK client). |
17	| `agent.json` | Sandbox config: `setup`, `run`, `models` (hosted models to wait for), optional `"browsers": 1-4`. |
18	| `tests/` | Unit tests against fakes. |
19	
20	`task` has `brief`, `access` (site ids, URLs, credentials), `submission` (`api` or `site`) and `answer_schema`.
21	For `api` submissions return the answer from `solve()`; for `site` submissions enter it on the website and return `None`.
22	
23	## Rules that decide whether a submission is accepted
24	
25	- A model must pick navigation targets and make decisions at runtime. No hardcoded answers, fixed scripts, crawlers
26	  or copied values. A coding agent reviews every package. Helpers (parsing, pagination of a model-selected result set,
27	  validation, form filling) are fine.
28	- A scored run lasts 20 min. Submit the best answer about 1 min before the end (`run.seconds_left(task)`); late = 0.
29	- Max 4 browsers, 4 vCPU / 8 GB RAM. The sandbox only reaches the platform and the websites.
30	- Package: max 20 MB compressed, `agent.json` at the root. Never include `.env` or keys (they are git-ignored).
31	- Hosted models are free, but each call adds simulated cost to ranking (quality, then cost x time). Use Qwen for
32	  easy steps; first call after idle can take several minutes, so use long timeouts.
33	
34	## Setup per laptop (once)
35	
36	Prerequisites: Git, Python is NOT required (uv manages 3.12), and a GitHub account that is on the Atira team.
37	
38	### Windows (PowerShell)
39	```powershell
40	irm https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/install.ps1 | iex          # Atira CLI (read the script first if you prefer)
41	winget install --id astral-sh.uv -e                           # uv
42	# open a NEW terminal so PATH updates
43	atira login                                                   # browser sign-in with GitHub
44	uv sync
45	uv run playwright install chromium
46	```
47	
48	### macOS / Linux
49	```sh
50	curl -fsSL https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/install.sh | sh     # Atira CLI; then add ~/.local/bin to PATH
51	curl -LsSf https://astral.sh/uv/install.sh | sh               # uv (or: brew install uv)
52	# open a NEW terminal
53	atira login
54	uv sync
55	uv run playwright install chromium        # on Linux add: uv run playwright install-deps chromium
56	```
57	
58	### Both: Claude Code helpers (optional)
59	```sh
60	claude mcp add atira -- atira mcp     # lets Claude read run logs, model calls, timings, compare runs
61	```
62	Check with `atira whoami`. Use `atira login --device` if no browser is available.
63	
64	## Develop locally
65	
66	Two terminals, both in the repo root.
67	
68	Terminal 1 (leave open): the free-model proxy.
69	```sh
70	atira models proxy
71	```
72	
73	Terminal 2: load scouting env, then run the agent.
74	```powershell
75	# Windows PowerShell
76	atira scout --env | Out-String | Invoke-Expression
77	uv run --no-sync python agent.py
78	```
79	```sh
80	# macOS / Linux
81	eval "$(atira scout --env)"
82	uv run --no-sync python agent.py
83	```
84	`atira scout --env` sets `CHALLENGE_SCOUTING`, `CHALLENGE_SITE_ACCESS`, site URLs and the `QWEN_*` / `CLEF_*`
85	variables pointing at the local proxy. The variables only live in that terminal. Local runs use the public
86	scouting logins: nothing done there is scored, and answers entered on the tender portal never count. Local model calls
87	are free and unranked. `atira scout` (no flag) prints the logins and brief for manual browsing.
88	
89	Unit tests: `uv run --no-sync python -m pytest tests -q` (add pytest with `uv add --dev pytest` if missing).
90	
91	## Test in the real sandbox
92	
93	```sh
94	atira test-run . --follow        # same sandbox as scored runs, public dataset, up to 2 h, not ranked
95	atira test-run . --dry-run       # only shows what would be packed (no upload)
96	```
97	Max 3 test runs waiting at once. Inspect results:
98	```sh
99	atira status                     # latest submissions and test runs
100	atira logs <run-id> --follow     # reh_... (test run) or run_... (scored run)
101	atira package <id>               # what was uploaded
102	atira cancel <run-id>
103	```
104	With the `atira` MCP server Claude can also fetch logs by time, model calls, where time went, browser screens and
105	compare two runs. Ask it "why did run reh_xxx fail?".
106	
107	## Submit (ranked, public)
108	
109	Run a test run first and make sure it finishes with a valid answer. Then agree in the team who submits
110	(one submission in flight per team, and it is public and final).
111	```sh
112	atira submit . --dry-run         # check the package
113	atira submit . --follow          # review -> one scored run on the public dataset -> leaderboard
114	atira leaderboard
115	```
116	The final ranking uses a private dataset with different websites and data, so build a general agent that does not
117	rely on public-dataset specifics. Choose the final attempt with `atira final [--best-of 1|3]` before the final run
118	starts (own model keys cost up to 3x).
119	
120	## Models
121	
122	- Default: hosted `qwen` (Qwen3.8-Flash-Next, up to 32 concurrent calls/team) via `models.qwen()`; `clef` (image
123	  decision model, 16 concurrent) via `models.ask_clef`. List every hosted model used in `agent.json` `"models"`.
124	- Own provider keys (Anthropic, OpenAI, ...) are stored as team secrets on the team page and go through the run's
125	  metering proxy. See the run contract, section LLM calls.
126	- Claude Code (this assistant) is only for writing code and runs on your own Claude. Optional experimental launcher
127	  `claude-atira` (Windows, per-user setup, not in the repo) points Claude Code at Qwen; plain `claude` is the default.
128	
129	## Team workflow
130	
131	- Commit with normal `git commit` / `git push` so Entire checkpoints get linked. Do not push `entire/*` branches.
132	- Never read, print or commit `.env` or API keys. `.entire/settings.json` is shared; `settings.local.json` is personal.
133	- Pull before starting, keep commits small, and say in the team chat before running `atira submit`.
134	
135	## Challenge overview: `rfq` v6 (source: challenge page, fair-play.md, run-contract.md; checked 2026-10-10)
136	
137	Goal: turn a public tender (German hydraulics manufacturer, hydraulic cylinders) into one correct, priced, **signed** bid
138	without human help. Answer is entered in the **tender-portal** configurator (`submission.kind = site`), signed with a TAN
139	from the webmail. Limits: answer 65,536 B, up to 100 positions, notes 4,000 chars.
140	
141	### The four sites (each run has its own logins; public scouting logins are unscored)
142	| Site | Holds | Traps |
143	| --- | --- | --- |
144	| `tender-portal` | tender, bill of quantities, bidder Q&A (changes quantities), bid configurator | cookie wall, flaky error pages, docs behind expression of interest, iframes, ZIPs, deadline in other timezone |
145	| `customer-portal` | buyer's technical spec + revisions | opens OLDEST revision first, nested viewers, paged tables |
146	| `erp` | materials, stock, lead times, price conditions | SAP-style transaction codes, F4 search popup, status codes, short session timeout (re-login) |
147	| `mail` | sales inbox: director's discount approval, signing TAN | look-alike/superseded approvals, archive folder, paging |
148	
149	### Bid rules (29 in the brief; the brief in `task["brief"]` is authoritative, re-read it every run)

... [63 lines truncated] ...

## atira
Atira Challenges: debug your team's agent system runs. Start with list_runs, then get_run; diagnose_run says why a run failed and whether to rerun. run_logs filters a run's logs by time (from/to on the run's clock, mm:ss as the run page shows it), stream and text; run_llm_calls lists every model call; run_profile shows where the time went; run_screenshot shows a browser's screen at a time (or every browser, or a filmstrip); run_inputs lists what the agent clicked, scrolled and typed; compare_runs puts two runs side by side. run_package shows the package a run or submission used (agent.json and its files) and saves it with out. test_run starts a test run from a folder; wait_for_run waits for it. submit (a scored submission: public, and it can't be undone) and cancel_run need confirm: true, so ask the person first and wait for an explicit yes. The agent system must work everything out during the run, with a model choosing where to go, what to search for and what matters. Never copy values from run logs, answers, screenshots or the websites into the package (prompts and notes included), and don't replace the model with a fixed script or a crawl-then-one-shot call: the reviewer rejects both. Rules at a glance: https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/docs/fair-play.md
